extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/patentees and attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examining and processing applications involving pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c) (CREATE Act) issues, joint research agreements, common ownership, provisional rejections, double patenting, and related biotechnological process (pre‑AIA 103(b)) elections. Covers applicant submission requirements, timing/fees, examiner actions, and remedies (e.g., terminal disclaimers, affidavits, petitions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint Research Agreement (JRA) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c)(3) defines a 'joint research agreement' as a written contract, grant, or cooperative agreement entered into by two or more persons or entities for the performance of experimental, developmental, or research work in the field of the claimed invention, that was in effect on or before the date the claimed invention was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The JRA must be a written agreement for research/development in the field of the claimed invention and be in effect on or before the date the later claimed invention was made. The JRA may predate the CREATE Act effective date (Dec. 10, 2004). The JRA is not required to be in effect on or before the prior art date of the reference sought to be disqualified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden to invoke JRA/common ownership to overcome prima facie obviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Once an examiner establishes a prima facie case of obviousness under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a), the burden of overcoming the rejection by invoking joint research agreement provisions (pre‑AIA 103(c)) or common ownership is on the applicant or patentee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants/patentees must comply with the statute and the applicable rules of practice to invoke disqualification under the CREATE Act; mere assertions without following statutory/rule procedures are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification amendment to disclose names of parties to a JRA (37 CFR 1.71(g)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification may disclose or be amended to disclose the names of the parties to a joint research agreement as defined in § 1.9(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments under 37 CFR 1.71(g)(1) are the means by which an application can disclose JRA parties when required by 35 U.S.C. 102(c) or pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c)(2)(C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and processing fee for 1.71(g) amendments (37 CFR 1.71(g)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment under 1.71(g)(1) must be accompanied by the processing fee set forth in § 1.17(i) if not filed within specified time periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exception time periods (no fee required) are: (i) within three months of filing date of a national application; (ii) within three months of entry of the national stage under § 1.491; (iii) before mailing of the first Office action on the merits; or (iv) before mailing of the first Office action after filing a request for continued examination under § 1.114. If filed outside these windows, submit processing fee per § 1.17(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of correction for late 1.71(g) amendments (37 CFR 1.71(g)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment under 1.71(g)(1) is filed after the issue fee is paid, the patent as issued may not include the names of the parties to the joint research agreement; correction must be by certificate of correction under 35 U.S.C. 255 and § 1.323 for the amendment to be effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent issues without the JRA party names because the amendment was after issue fee payment (or after grant), a certificate of correction (35 U.S.C. 255 and § 1.323) is required; a reissue or reexamination is unnecessary solely to add omitted JRA names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement to treat subject matter as commonly owned (37 CFR 1.104(c)(5)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: To be treated as commonly owned for purposes of pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c) (in effect prior to March 16, 2013), the applicant or patent owner must provide a statement that the subject matter and the claimed invention, at the time the claimed invention was made, were owned by the same person or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement is the procedural mechanism to invoke common ownership disqualification; follow form and signature rules (see related rubric on statement form).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement content for JRA disqualification (37 CFR 1.104(c)(5)(ii)(A)-(B))
rubrics_metrics.description: To invoke JRA‑based disqualification under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c)(2), the applicant/patent owner must provide: (A) a statement that the subject matter and the claimed invention were made by or on behalf of the parties to a JRA (within 35 U.S.C. 100(h) and § 1.9(e)) that was in effect on or before the date the claimed invention was made and that the claimed invention was made as a result of activities undertaken within the scope of the JRA; and (B) the application for the claimed invention discloses or is amended to disclose the names of the parties to the JRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both content elements are required: the factual statement about who made the inventions and that the invention resulted from activities within the JRA, plus disclosure (or timely amendment) of the JRA party names in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and signature requirements for common ownership/JRA statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The required statement should either be on or begin on a separate sheet and must not be directed to other matters (37 CFR 1.4(c)). The statement must be signed in accordance with 37 CFR 1.33(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow filing format rules: separate sheet, limited content, and proper signature; improper form or signature may affect acceptance of the statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence supporting JRA existence optional
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant or patent owner may, but is not required to, present evidence supporting the existence of the joint research agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statutory/rule statement is the primary instrument — documentary evidence may be submitted but is not mandated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of proper submission: treatment of prior art as commonly owned
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant disqualifies the subject matter relied upon by the examiner in accordance with pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c) and the rules, the examiner will treat the application under examination and the pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e),(f), or (g) prior art as if they are commonly owned for purposes of pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper statutory/rule-compliant submissions result in disqualification and changes in how the examiner applies 103(a) rejections (i.e., treat as commonly owned).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions required for disqualification of a reference used in anticipatory rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference used in an anticipatory rejection under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e),(f), or (g) is disqualified only when: (A) a proper submission is filed; (B) the reference only qualifies as prior art under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e),(f) or (g) (i.e., not under 102(a) or (b)); and (C) the reference was used in an obviousness rejection under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All three conditions must be satisfied for disqualification to operate; if any condition is lacking, the reference remains prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner procedure when common ownership/JRA NOT established
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application file has not established that the reference is disqualified under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c), the examiner will: (A) assume the reference is not disqualified; (B) examine the application on all grounds other than any conflict arising from a potential 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection based on 102(e),(f) and/or (g); (C) consider applicability of references under 103 based on 102(e),(f) and/or (g), including provisional rejections; and (D) apply the best references against the claimed invention by rejections under 102 and 103(a) until the reference is disqualified under 103(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should anticipate possible later disqualification and consider making alternative/additional rejections. If a statement of common ownership is filed in reply to a 103(a) rejection and claims are not amended, the examiner may not make the next Office action final if a new rejection is made (MPEP §706.07(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to enter 1.71(g) amendment without terminal disclaimer when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment under 37 CFR 1.71(g) is submitted in an application under final rejection to overcome a 103(a) rejection based upon a U.S. patent that qualifies as prior art only under pre‑AIA 102(e), the examiner may refuse to enter the amendment if it is not accompanied by an appropriate terminal disclaimer (37 CFR 1.321(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such amendments can necessitate reopening prosecution (e.g., for entry of a nonstatutory double patenting rejection). If a terminal disclaimer is required but not submitted, the amendment can be refused entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner procedure when common ownership/JRA HAS been established
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application has established that the reference is disqualified under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c), the examiner will: (A) examine the applications as to all grounds except pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e),(f) and (g) (as they apply through 103(a)); (B) examine for double patenting (statutory and nonstatutory) and make provisional double patenting rejections if appropriate; and (C) invite the applicant to file a terminal disclaimer to overcome provisional or actual nonstatutory double patenting rejections, if appropriate (see 37 CFR 1.321).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once disqualification is established, the examiner shifts focus away from 102(e)/(f)/(g) prior art and toward double patenting and related remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double patenting treatment under CREATE Act
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendment of pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c) by the CREATE Act can create double patenting rejections between applications not owned by the same party; for double patenting analysis, the application/patent and the subject matter disqualified under 103(c) will be treated as if commonly owned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonstatutory double patenting rejections prevent multiple patents with different expiration dates covering nearly identical subject matter. Nonstatutory double patenting can be overcome by filing a terminal disclaimer under 37 CFR 1.321, including provisions tying enforceability term to common ownership. For non‑commonly owned patents treated as commonly owned due to CREATE Act, the rejection may be obviated by filing the appropriate terminal disclaimer per 37 CFR 1.321(d). See MPEP §§804, 804.02, 1490.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional rejection (obviousness) under 35 U.S.C. 103(a) using provisional prior art (pre‑AIA 102(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where two applications of different inventive entities are copending, unpublished, and the filing dates differ, a provisional rejection under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) based on provisional prior art under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) should be made in the later filed application unless the application has been disqualified under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain confidentiality under 35 U.S.C. 122. The provisional rejection alerts the applicant to expect a nonprovisional rejection if one application issues and provides opportunity to avoid loss of rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options to overcome provisional 103(a) rejection (copending applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional 103(a) rejection based on provisional prior art under pre‑AIA 102(e) can be overcome by: (A) arguing patentability over the earlier filed application; (B) combining subject matter into a single application claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 and abandoning copending applications (subject to 112/enablement concerns); (C) filing an affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.132 showing derivation; (D) filing an affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131(a) showing date of invention prior to the provisional 102(e) date; or (E) for applications pending on or after Dec. 10, 2004, showing common ownership at time invention was made or that subject matter is disqualified under pre‑AIA 103(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each option has legal/formal prerequisites (e.g., 1.132 derivation evidence, 1.131 date of invention proof, 35 U.S.C. 120 benefit requirements and 35 U.S.C. 112 compliance). Combining applications may affect entitlement to earlier filing dates (Studiengesellschaft Kohle v. Shell Oil).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of terminal disclaimer and affidavits for interfering subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applications claim interfering subject matter (37 CFR 41.203(a)), a terminal disclaimer and an affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131(c) may be used to overcome a 103(a) rejection in a common ownership situation if the earlier application has been published or matured into a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 718 for guidance on interfering subject matter and proper use of terminal disclaimers/affidavits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of combining copending applications into a single application
rubrics_metrics.description: If copending applications are combined into a single application and the combined application is subject to a restriction requirement, a proper divisional application would not be subject to a provisional or nonprovisional 103(a) rejection in view of the combined application because 35 U.S.C. 121 would preclude the use of a patent issuing from the combined application as a reference against the divisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The combined application can be a continuation‑in‑part entitled to 35 U.S.C. 120 benefit of the prior applications; this strategy can avoid provisional 103 rejections but has implications for claim entitlement and restriction practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(b) (biotechnological processes) eligibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre‑AIA 103(b) provides that a biotechnological process using or resulting in a composition of matter that is novel under 102 and nonobvious under 103(a) shall be considered nonobvious if, upon timely election: (A) claims to the process and the composition are contained in the same application or in separate applications having the same effective filing date; and (B) the composition and the process at the time invented were owned by the same person or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person. A patent issued on a process under paragraph (1) must also contain the composition claims used in or made by the process, or if composition claimed in another patent, the patents must expire on the same date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain 103(b) treatment the applicant must timely petition under 37 CFR 1.182 and establish satisfaction of all statutory requirements. If process and composition are in different patents, expiration dates must be aligned. Election procedures and timing rules (see related rubric) must be followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'biotechnological process' for 103(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of 103(b), a 'biotechnological process' means: (A) a process of genetically altering or otherwise inducing a single‑ or multi‑celled organism to (i) express an exogenous nucleotide sequence, (ii) inhibit, eliminate, augment, or alter expression of an endogenous nucleotide sequence, or (iii) express a specific physiological characteristic not naturally associated with the organism; (B) cell fusion procedures yielding a cell line that expresses a specific protein (e.g., monoclonal antibody); and other enumerated biotech process types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process claims must fall within the statutory definition to qualify for 103(b) treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and procedure for election under pre‑AIA 103(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: An election to proceed under pre‑AIA 103(b) shall be made by petition under 37 CFR 1.182. The petition must establish that all statutory requirements are satisfied. An election will normally be timely if made no later than the earlier of either payment of the issue fee or filing of an appeal brief in an application that contains a composition claim which has not been rejected under 102 or 103(a). For certain applications pending in specified dates, other timing rules (37 CFR 1.312(b)) may apply. If a patent issued without an election due to error, a reissue application may be filed to permit consideration of eligible process claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow petition rules and timing carefully; late or defective elections can be fatal to obtaining 103(b) benefit, though reissue may be possible in some error cases.
